prac.prompt: Which pair are BOTH multicellular?

options.fb: Both are made of many cells.

prac.prompt: An elephant and a mouse are both mammals. Why is an adult elephant bigger?

options.t: It has many more cells, not much bigger cells
options.fb: Correct – organisms grow mostly by increasing cell number.

options.t: Its cells are thousands of times bigger
options.fb: Cells of different mammals are roughly similar in size.
Each body cell normally has one nucleus.

prac.prompt: Eyepiece ×15, objective ×10. What is the total magnification? (type the number only)
A microscope gives ×400. The objective is ×40. What is the eyepiece magnification?

errs.fb: You multiplied. Divide total by objective: 400 ÷ 40.
Subtracting is wrong – total = eyepiece × objective, so eyepiece = 400 ÷ 40.

prac.prompt: Why did scientists need microscopes to develop cell theory?

options.t: Most cells are too small to see with the naked eye
Cells only exist under a microscope
options.fb: Cells exist everywhere in living things.

options.t: Microscopes change the colour of cells

prac.prompt: Order these discoveries from earliest to latest.
items: Ibn al-Haytham explains how lenses work (about 1021)
Schleiden and Schwann state cell theory (1839)
Virchow adds 'cells come from pre-existing cells'

prac.prompt: Schleiden studied plants and Schwann studied animals. Why was sharing their findings important?

options.t: Together they showed BOTH plants and animals are made of cells, so the idea applied to all living things
options.fb: Correct – evidence from two groups made the theory general.

options.t: They proved cells come from pre-existing cells

prac.prompt: Match each microscope part with its job.

pairs.r: magnifies the specimen, close to the slide
small focus changes at high power

prac.prompt: A student's specimen is too thick and nothing can be seen clearly. What is the most likely reason?

options.t: Light cannot pass through a thick specimen
options.fb: A light microscope needs light to pass THROUGH the specimen.
Clips hold the slide; they don't affect clarity this way.
A coverslip helps, but thickness is the main problem.

prac.prompt: Why must a microscope mirror never point at the Sun?

options.t: Sunlight focused into the eye can permanently damage eyesight

options.fb: The danger is to the eye.

options.t: Cells only show up in lamp light

prac.prompt: An image of a pollen grain is 12 mm long under a ×400 microscope. What is its real length in mm?

errs.fb: You multiplied. Image is bigger than real, so real = image ÷ magnification.

prac.unitFb: Image in mm → real size in mm.

prac.prompt: Select ALL examples of unicellular organisms.
What is a microorganism?

options.t: An organism so small you need a microscope to see it

options.fb: Parts of cells are not organisms.
Yeast, Amoeba and others are microorganisms too.

prac.prompt: Cell theory changed when Virchow added a third statement. What does this show about science?

options.t: Scientific theories can change when new evidence is found

options.fb: They worked with the evidence they had.

options.t: Only one scientist can build a theory

prac.prompt: Cells look flat under a microscope. What should you remember?

options.fb: Correct – we see a thin slice / one focal plane.
The coverslip flattens a little, but cells are 3D.

prac.prompt: Fill in the missing magnifications.
head: Eyepiece
Objective
Total

prac.prompt: A student swaps the ×10 objective for ×40. What happens to the field of view (area seen)?

options.t: It becomes smaller, showing fewer cells but bigger
It becomes larger, showing more cells
options.fb: Higher magnification shows a smaller area.
It usually becomes darker at high power.

prac.prompt: Van Leeuwenhoek's lenses magnified about ×200. Hooke's compound microscope used two lenses. Which statement is correct?

options.t: A compound microscope has two lenses in a tube
Compound microscopes have only one lens
Van Leeuwenhoek could not see unicellular organisms

options.fb: Magnification has no unit – we write ×200.

prac.prompt: Match each part with its function.

pairs.r: controls all cell activities; contains DNA
jelly where materials are made and broken down
controls what goes in and out
takes in water to keep the cell firm

prac.prompt: Which statement about the cell wall is FALSE?

options.t: It controls exactly which substances enter the cell
options.fb: Correct – this is FALSE: the MEMBRANE controls entry.

options.t: Animal cells do not have one

prac.prompt: Why is iodine solution added to onion cells on a slide?

options.t: To stain parts so they are easier to see

prac.prompt: Dodder is a plant with NO green parts. It grows on other plants. What do its cells lack, and how does it get food?

options.t: Chloroplasts – it takes nutrients from its host plant
Cell walls – it absorbs food through its skin
Nuclei – it gets food from soil

prac.prompt: Select ALL safety rules when making a cheek cell slide.

options.t: Only use cells from your own body
Put the cotton bud in disinfectant right after use
Wear eye protection when using coverslips/stain
Share cotton buds with a partner to save materials
Taste the methylene blue to check it

prac.prompt: In a plant cell, why does the cytoplasm form only a thin layer?

options.t: The large sap vacuole takes up most of the space
Plant cells have less cytoplasm because they are dead

prac.prompt: Which part is NOT visible with a school light microscope?

options.fb: Correct – DNA is inside the nucleus but too small.

prac.prompt: Which cell type has each feature?
Algae are unicellular, live in water and contain chloroplasts. Which statement is correct?

options.t: They can photosynthesise, but they are not plants because plants are multicellular
They are animals because they move
options.fb: Movement alone doesn't classify them as animals.

options.t: They are plants because they have chloroplasts
options.fb: Plants are multicellular; algae here are unicellular.

prac.prompt: A student's onion drawing shows a cell with chloroplasts. The teacher marks it wrong. Why?

options.t: Onion bulb cells have no chloroplasts – the student copied the model, not the specimen

prac.prompt: What is the main job of the sap vacuole?

options.t: Takes in water to keep the cell firm

prac.prompt: Match the stain/tool with its use.
Why is the coverslip lowered slowly at an angle with a mounted needle?

options.t: To stop air bubbles being trapped

prac.prompt: Cheek cells on a slide are spread randomly and have irregular shapes. Why?

options.t: Animal cells have no cell wall, so their shape is not fixed, and scraping separates them

options.fb: Animal cells don't have large vacuoles.

prac.prompt: Select ALL parts that release or capture energy.
A model cell is built from jelly (cytoplasm), a grape (nucleus) and a plastic bag (membrane). What is one weakness?

options.t: It does not show mitochondria or other parts and is far too big
The jelly is a good cytoplasm

prac.prompt: Which part contains the instructions (DNA) passed from parents to offspring?
Read the volume of methylene blue in this measuring cylinder.

errs.fb: From 6 to 8 mL there are 4 spaces, so each space is 0.5 mL. Count again.
You read one space too many. Each space = 0.5 mL.

prac.prompt: A root hair cell has NO chloroplasts. Why?

options.t: It is underground in the dark, so it cannot photosynthesise

prac.prompt: Which feature gives a red blood cell a LARGE surface area?
Why do some neurones need to be up to 1 metre long?

options.t: To carry impulses quickly over long distances, e.g. from the spine to the foot

prac.prompt: Match the cell to where it is found.
'Multicellular organisms are made of just one type of cell.' Is this true?

options.t: No – they have many types of specialised cells
Yes – all cells are the same
options.fb: Cells differ in shape and job.
Plants also have many cell types.

prac.prompt: Muscle cells change shape to lift your bag. What would muscle cells need lots of?

options.fb: Muscle cells must change shape – no wall.

prac.prompt: Select ALL specialised PLANT cells.
A person has fewer red blood cells than normal. Which symptom is most likely?

options.t: Feeling tired because less oxygen reaches body cells

prac.prompt: Which change would make a root hair cell absorb water MORE slowly?
Palisade cells are tall and column-shaped. How does this help?

options.t: Many can pack closely side by side to absorb lots of light

prac.prompt: Put the steps of the lung's cleaning system in order.
items: Air with dust is breathed in
Mucus moves away from the lungs

prac.prompt: What is haemoglobin?

options.t: A red pigment that carries oxygen

options.fb: It's a substance in red blood cells.

prac.prompt: Which cell would be MOST affected by a chemical that stops cilia beating?

options.t: Ciliated cell in the air passages

prac.prompt: Plant or animal specialised cell?
A new cell is found with a huge folded membrane and many tiny finger-like projections. What is its most likely job?

options.fb: Correct – large surface area = fast absorption.

prac.prompt: Why does division of labour make an organism efficient?

options.t: Each cell type is specialised and does its own job very well
All cells do every job at once
It reduces the number of cells

prac.prompt: Where are the branched endings of a neurone and what do they do?

options.t: At the ends of the cell; they receive messages from other cells
Inside the nucleus; they store DNA
On the surface; they trap dust
In the blood; they carry oxygen

prac.prompt: Describe how the structure of a palisade cell is related to its function.

rubric.pt: Many chloroplasts to absorb light energy.
Near the upper surface where most light falls → photosynthesis.

supports the plant; moves water up and food around

options.fb: The book shows six of the 11.
That's the number of bones in an adult.

prac.prompt: Which TWO organ systems work together to deliver oxygen to muscle cells?

options.fb: Lungs take in oxygen; blood carries it.
Blood is needed to carry oxygen.

prac.prompt: Which of these is an ORGAN SYSTEM in plants?
What feature of plant cells would NOT be found in root cells? Why?

options.t: Chloroplasts – roots grow in the dark and do not photosynthesise

Which organ controls all body functions, including what we think and feel?

Which system does each organ belong to?

options.t: So the whole organism functions efficiently
Because each system can do every job

options.t: The heart is an organ made of muscle tissue and other tissues
The heart is a single giant muscle cell

prac.prompt: Select ALL the organs.
In a tall tree, water reaches the top leaves. Which tissue makes this possible?
Sunflower seeds are made in the ovary of the flower. Which level is the ovary?

options.fb: Correct – the book uses ovaries as an example of an organ.
It's part of the reproductive system.

prac.prompt: Which organ system breaks down food and absorbs nutrients into the blood?
Give an example of how TWO organ systems work together when you run.

rubric.pt: Name two systems (e.g. muscular + skeletal, respiratory + circulatory).
Describe what each does in the example.
Explain the link (one system helps the other).

prac.model: When you run, the muscular system contracts muscles that pull on the bones of the skeletal system, so the legs move. The respiratory system takes in more oxygen and the circulatory system carries it to the muscle cells for energy.
